note: No reference/topologies/linear-regulator.md exists yet in this library; this file is the seed of one. Design point: 5V in (4.75-5.25) -> 3.3V/500mA continuous out, 0.975W dissipation at Ta=50C still air, 2-layer JLC board, block-only scope.

decisions.what: AMS1117-class and LM1117 are ESR-DEPENDENT: output cap must be tantalum or aluminum electrolytic within a stated ESR window, not bare ceramic.
decisions.why: LM1117 datasheet states min 10uF tantalum output cap, ESR must range 0.3-22 ohm. AMS1117 clone datasheet states 10uF tantalum or 50uF aluminum electrolytic, ESR must not exceed 0.5 ohm. Neither qualifies a ceramic-only solution; an all-ceramic BOM (ESR typically <0.05 ohm) falls below both windows and risks oscillation.
decisions.source: TI LM1117 SNOS412Q s.9.2.2.1.3 'Output Capacitor' p.15 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm1117.pdf); Slkor AMS1117 datasheet p.5 'Output Capacitor' (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/8122/AMS11173.3SOT223.pdf)

decisions.what: MIC29302A is ESR-TOLERANT and explicitly warns extremely-low-ESR ceramic MAY CONTRIBUTE TO INSTABILITY; stable with 10uF at full load, aluminum electrolytic adequate, tantalum recommended only for fast transient response.
decisions.why: Inverse of the 1117-class trap: this part does not need ESR-boosted caps, but pairing it with a bare low-ESR ceramic is called out by the vendor as a risk, not a benefit.
decisions.source: Microchip MIC29302A datasheet Rev 2.0 p.11 'Capacitor Requirements' (https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/MIC29302A.pdf)

decisions.what: AP2114 (CMOS pass device) is genuinely ceramic-stable: datasheet states stable with 4.7uF ceramic, tantalum, or aluminum electrolytic, and the electrical-characteristics table is measured with CIN=COUT=4.7uF ceramic.
decisions.why: Different internal compensation (CMOS pass FET) from the bipolar/PNP parts above; this is the only surveyed part where an all-ceramic BOM is both claimed AND the vendor's own test condition.
decisions.source: BCD Semiconductor AP2114 datasheet Rev 1.3 p.1 Features, p.6 Electrical Characteristics test conditions (https://www1.futureelectronics.com/doc/BCD%20SEMICONDUCTOR/AP2114H-2.5TRG1.pdf)

decisions.what: theta_JA is copper-area-dependent and package/copper-weight dependent; LM1117's own sweep for SOT-223 (1oz) runs 136 C/W at bare pad down to 66 C/W at 1 in^2 top-side copper; TO-252 (2oz) runs 103 down to 47 C/W over the same area grid.
decisions.why: This is the primary driver of what board outline/copper this design needs to earn at P6/P7 - a single headline theta_JA number is not sufficient to size the board.
decisions.source: TI LM1117 SNOS412Q Table 9-2, Figures 9-11/9-12/9-13/9-14, pp.18-19 (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm1117.pdf)

decisions.what: Bottom-side (via-fed) copper is roughly 20% LESS effective per unit area than top-side copper for these non-exposed-pad packages (SOT-223, TO-252), because the tab solders to the top layer and vias add thermal resistance to reach the bottom.
decisions.why: Directly answers 'how much does a 2-layer bottom pour really buy': less than the same area of top copper, by about a fifth, for this package class. At matched 1 in^2: SOT-223 66 (top) vs 79 C/W (bottom); TO-252 47 (top) vs 57 C/W (bottom).
decisions.source: TI LM1117 SNOS412Q Table 9-2 layouts 6 vs 11, p.18-19

decisions.what: MIC29302A's headline theta_JA (TO-252=35 C/W, TO-263=28 C/W) is explicitly conditioned on 2oz copper AND >=100mm^2 (0.155 in^2) copper area, not JEDEC 1 in^2 - a much smaller area point than TI's sweep uses.
decisions.why: Vendor headline theta_JA numbers are not comparable across parts without checking what copper condition each one assumed; this number looks better than LM1117's TO-252-at-1in^2 (47 C/W) partly because of package/die differences, not because it needs less copper in an absolute sense.
decisions.source: Microchip MIC29302A datasheet Rev 2.0 p.3 Package Thermal Resistance table, p.10 'Thermal Design' worked example (https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/DeviceDoc/MIC29302A.pdf)

decisions.what: AMS1117 clone datasheet gives only a single bare-minimum-pad theta_JA (SOT-223=150 C/W, TO-252=125 C/W, SOT89=225 C/W) with no copper-area statement at all - worse than even TI's 'pad only' data point for the same package (136 C/W).
decisions.why: A single headline theta_JA number, unqualified by copper area, should be treated as a worst case, not a design target; use a copper-area sweep or an explicit stated criterion instead.
decisions.source: Slkor AMS1117 datasheet p.2 Absolute Maximum Ratings table

decisions.what: AP2114 datasheet gives ONLY theta_JC (junction-to-case: SOT-223=50.9, TO-252-2=35, TO-263-3=22 C/W), never theta_JA - the board's contribution is not characterized by the vendor at all.
decisions.why: A design using AP2114 cannot size copper from the datasheet alone and must fall back to a generic thermal model or bench measurement; this is a gap to flag at P2/P3, not a usable thermal decision.
decisions.source: BCD Semiconductor AP2114 datasheet Rev 1.3 p.6 Electrical Characteristics, 'Thermal Resistance (Junction to Case)' row

decisions.what: Tab/thermal-pad electrical identity differs by part and is NOT uniform: LM1117 and AMS1117 (3-pin SOT-223/TO-252) have TAB = VOUT; MIC29302A (5-pin TO-263/TO-252, ADJ output) has TAB = GND (internally tied).
decisions.why: Determines whether the heatsink copper pour is a 'hot' output island needing isolation from other copper, or can be tied directly into the board's GND fill. Must be confirmed per the exact chosen part before laying out the pour.
decisions.source: TI LM1117 SNOS412Q Figures 6-1..6-4 p.3 ('Tab is VOUT'); Slkor AMS1117 p.2 pinout (same convention); Microchip MIC29302A p.2 Pin Description ('GND: TAB is also connected internally to the IC's ground on both packages')

layout_notes.what: Input capacitor at the VIN pin with short leads is the universal baseline across all four candidate classes; none of the four datasheets calls out a hot-loop or Kelvin-sense requirement beyond this - linear regulators have no switch node.
layout_notes.source: TI LM1117 p.14; Slkor AMS1117 p.5; Microchip MIC29302A p.11

layout_notes.what: MIC29302A's own eval-board layout places input caps (ceramic+tantalum) and output caps (ceramic+tantalum) immediately flanking the IC on the top layer with a dedicated PGND pour; no analog/power ground split shown (single simple rail, no feedback-noise-sensitive stage).
layout_notes.source: Microchip MIC29302A datasheet Rev 2.0 pp.14-15 'PCB Layout Recommendations'

layout_notes.what: If a fixed-output part is chosen (satisfies the +/-3% accuracy spec per requirements.md answer 5), no external feedback divider is needed and the ADJ-pin placement rules below do not apply.

If an adjustable part is chosen instead: keep the CADJ bypass-impedance rule 1/(2*pi*fRIPPLE*CADJ) < R1, and size R1+R2 low enough to pass the part's own minimum-load spec through the divider if the divider is the only load path.
layout_notes.source: TI LM1117 s.9.2.2.1.2 p.14-15; Slkor AMS1117 p.5; Microchip MIC29302A p.11 'Adjustable Regulator Design'

errata.what: AMS1117 clone dropout is 1.30V typ / 1.40V max AT 1A per this vendor's own table - worse than the ~1.1V figure commonly repeated online for 'AMS1117'. No 500mA point is tabulated explicitly, only 1A guaranteed.
errata.source: Slkor AMS1117 datasheet p.3 Electrical Characteristics table

errata.what: AP2114 dropout figures conflict between sources fetched: front page states 450mV typ @1A for the 3.3V variant, but the electrical table retrieved (AP2114-1.2 variant only, Vin=2.5V test condition) shows 1200/1300mV typ/max at 1A - different Vout variant and test Vin, not directly comparable. UNCONFIRMED against the -3.3 variant's own table; refetch before relying on the 450mV figure if AP2114 is selected.
errata.source: BCD Semiconductor AP2114 datasheet Rev 1.3 p.1 Features vs p.6 Electrical Characteristics (AP2114-1.2 table)

errata.what: Minimum load current is NOT uniform across the candidate class: AMS1117 3mA typ/10mA max (all variants), MIC29302A 10mA min (all variants), but LM1117 FIXED-output variants have no stated min-load spec at all (only the ADJ variant does, 1.7/5mA) - relevant since this board's static resistive load could sit near zero at bench idle.
errata.source: TI LM1117 SNOS412Q p.6 Electrical Characteristics table footnote 5; Slkor AMS1117 p.3; Microchip MIC29302A p.11 'Minimum Load Current'

errata.what: Quiescent/ground current is not flat vs load for every topology: MIC29302A (PNP pass) ground current scales with output current (~2% of Iout per the vendor's own PD formula, 5mA typ at 750mA out rising to 60mA typ at 3A out), while AP2114 (CMOS pass) stays a near-constant 60uA typ regardless of load.
errata.source: Microchip MIC29302A datasheet p.3 Ground Current table, p.10 PD formula; BCD AP2114 datasheet p.6 Quiescent Current row

errata.what: Thermal shutdown thresholds differ across the class: AMS1117 150C (10C hysteresis), MIC29302A 125C, AP2114 160C (25C hysteresis), LM1117 125C recommended max junction. requirements.md's '~75 C/W or better for a 125C part' framing is conservative (extra margin available) for AMS1117/AP2114's higher thresholds - but design to 125C Tj max regardless, since shutdown is a fault response not a steady-state target.
errata.source: Slkor AMS1117 p.3; Microchip MIC29302A p.10; BCD AP2114 p.6; TI LM1117 s.9.5.1.1 p.18

errata.what: Counterfeit/clone variance is real and specific to AMS1117-class jellybean parts: the datasheet retrieved for 'AMS1117' is branded Slkor, a second-source/clone die, not the original Advanced Monolithic Systems part. The part number is used by many fabs with non-identical dies - pin the exact manufacturer/part number in the BOM if this class is chosen; do not assume datasheet numbers transfer across suppliers.
errata.source: Slkor AMS1117 datasheet cover page (self-identifies as Slkor, not AMS)

errata.what: Project-internal fact (not a vendor citation): this repo's check_thermal gate uses a first-principles copper-spreader theta_JA model, validated to within 5% of a vendor JEDEC number elsewhere in the project; board AREA dominates theta_JA more than inner-layer copper weight for small boards. Relevant because board_edit --outline fit (P6/P7) sizes this board's outline against that model, not directly against the vendor tables above.
